To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the developmental expression of GluA1/2 and GluA4 subunits is essential for the proper synchronization of the CA1 and CA3 neuronal populations during the first week after birth.
GluA4 is necessary for the development of functional coupling between CA3 and CA 1 neuronal populations in the hippocampus.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of the hippocampus, a brain structure which plays a key role in learning and memory.
the developmentally specific mechanisms of plasticity at the hippocampal CA3–CA 1 synapses.
the mechanisms underlying the development of the hippocampus and its functional role in the brain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
GluA4 plays a role in the development of the hippocampus, but it is unclear whether this role is direct or indirect.
GluA4 dependent plasticity mechanisms contribute to development of the hippocampus by synchronizing CA3–CA3 and CA1–CA1 neuronal activity.
the loss of Glu4 does not affect the overall excitability but impairs the functional coupling of the CA3-CA1 neuronal population in the immature hippocampi.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the GluA4 dependent synaptic plasticity mechanisms are important for the developmental maturation of the hippocampus.
GluA4 dependent plasticity mechanisms are important for the development of the hippocampus and that loss of Glu4 may contribute to the pathogenesis of schizophrenia and other disorders.
the developmental GluA4 dependent synaptic plasticity mechanisms are essential for the functional maturation of the CA3-CA1 circuitry in the hippocampus.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the developmentally restricted synaptic plasticity mechanisms can have significant impact on the functional development of neuronal networks.
GluA4 dependent synaptic plasticity mechanisms contribute to the development of the CA3-CA1 circuitry and may be important for normal brain development and function.

the developmental plasticity mechanisms are not merely a transient feature of the early development but rather play an active role in establishing and maintaining functional connectivity between neuronal sub-population in the hippocampal network.
